label: Matrix
terms_note: Open standard, no vendor gate — the homeserver operator's terms apply (matrix.org's own server for example forbids spam). Auth: legacy POST /login (m.login.password, m.login.sso, …) or the OAuth 2.0 API (authorization code / device flows); `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` (query-string token deprecated). Rate limiting is per homeserver: M_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with retry_after_ms (Retry-After header preferred). Bots / bridges are first-class in the ecosystem (Application Service API for puppeting is a separate spec).

sdks: matrix-org / element-hq client SDKs (matrix-js-sdk, matrix-rust-sdk, matrix-nio for Python) — spec.matrix.org lists the API; SDKs are ecosystem projects, not required

endpoints.call: PUT /rooms/{roomId}/send/m.room.message/{txnId}` `{msgtype: m.text, body, format, formatted_body, m.relates_to}
endpoints.purpose: send; `m.relates_to {rel_type: m.thread, event_id}` for threads; `m.in_reply_to` for replies

reference.limits: - Rate limiting is homeserver policy: `429 M_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` with `retry_after_ms` (prefer the `Retry-After` header). - No vendor terms — the homeserver operator's acceptable-use applies (matrix.org forbids spam). Bots and bridges are ordinary clients; puppeting other users needs the Application Service API (separate spec, homeserver-admin registration). - `txnId` idempotency on every send; `/sync` `since` token is the cursor.

fields.name: access_token
fields.help: Access token of the account (from a login flow or the client's settings), sent as 'Authorization: Bearer' — 'Access tokens may be provided via a request header, using the Authentication Bearer scheme: Authorization: Bearer TheTokenHere' (https://spec.matrix.org/latest/client-server-api/#using-access-tokens).

config_fields.name: homeserver
config_fields.help: Host of the account's homeserver client API without scheme (e.g. matrix.org, or the m.homeserver base_url from /.well-known/matrix/client without https://); every call goes to https://<homeserver>/_matrix/client/... Env: PLATFORM_MCP_MATRIX_HOMESERVER.

adapter.rate_note: Homeservers rate-limit per their own policy and answer 429 with errcode M_LIMIT_EXCEEDED and retry_after_ms (https://spec.matrix.org/latest/client-server-api/#rate-limiting); the spec sets no numbers, so the client bucket is the runtime default 2/s.

me.note: 'Gets information about the owner of a given access token' — account carries user_id (required), device_id and is_guest.

send.note: 'This endpoint is used to send a message event to a room': `to` is the ROOM id (!id:server) the account has joined, not a user id (a DM is a room too); `text` is sent as an m.room.message with msgtype m.text ('This message is the most basic message and is used to represent text'); `subject` and `channel` are ignored. The runtime generates a fresh UUID per call as the txnId ('Clients should generate an ID unique across requests with the same access token; it will be used by the server to ensure idempotency of requests'), so retries by the caller are new events. message_id is the event_id.

reply.note: A threaded reply is an m.room.message whose content carries m.relates_to {rel_type: m.thread, event_id: <thread root>} plus the fallback fields (is_falling_back: true, m.in_reply_to: {event_id}) the threading section asks clients to include for non-threaded clients: `thread_id` is the thread root event id ($...) and `channel` (the room id) is REQUIRED — the same PUT .../rooms/{roomId}/send/m.room.message/{txnId} as send, with a fresh UUID txnId per call. Replying to a message that is not yet a thread root starts a thread on it. message_id is the new event_id.

list_inbound.note: Lists ONE room: `channel` is the room id (!id:server) and is REQUIRED — there is no cross-room inbox endpoint (that is /sync, a long-poll). dir=b with no `from` returns the newest events first ('If it is not provided, the homeserver shall return a list of messages from the first or last (per the value of the dir parameter) visible event in the room history for the requesting user'); the server pages by start / end tokens, so `page` is ignored and only the newest `limit` ('Default: 10') events are returned; `since` is not sent. Every room event is a row: state events and non-text messages have no content.body (see raw.type / raw.content); `thread_id` is the room id; origin_server_ts is Unix ms under raw.

get_thread.note: 'Retrieve all of the child events for a given parent event which relate to the parent using the given relType', with relType m.thread: `thread_id` is the thread root event id ($...) and `channel` (the room id) is REQUIRED. Events come 'ordered topologically most-recent first'; the root event itself is not included; the server pages by next_batch, so `page` is ignored and only `limit` events are returned ('The server can and should apply a maximum value to this parameter'). `thread_id` on each row is the room id; the root is under raw.content['m.relates_to'].event_id.

mark_read.note: 'This API updates the marker for the given receipt type to the event ID specified' with receipt type m.read (public read receipt): `channel` (the room id) and `message_id` ('The event ID to acknowledge up to') are both required; `thread_id` is not used (no request body is sent, so the receipt is unthreaded — 'If not specified, the read receipt is unthreaded (default)'). Matrix answers an empty object; status is the literal 'read'.
